Title: Qud Expanded Community Edition
Description:
[h1]Qud Expanded Community Edition[/h1]
[i]A community-maintained fork of [b]Caves of Qud Expanded[/b] by Mura.[/i]

This is a [b]separate mod[/b]. It does not replace, modify, or take over the original, which remains Mura's and is still available here:
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1134036260]Caves of Qud Expanded[/url]

[h1]What you get[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Psionic Adept[/b] — a third genotype for players who would rather find their build than plan it. No mutations, the fewest stat points in the game, the most skill points per level of anyone, and power that comes from psionic chips: they cannot be bought or built, and only ever come out of chests. A True Kin saves up for the implant it wants; an Adept wears what it finds. 18 subtypes, casters and martial guardians, with sprites by Noble Lark.
[*][b]144 psionic chips[/b] — implantable chips that grant real mutations to genotypes that cannot mutate. Every one of them can be found.
[*][b]Complete weapon and armor families[/b] — bronze through zetachrome, one- and two-handed, with consistent stats and prices across every tier.
[*][b]New weapon classes[/b] — katanas, rapiers, halberds, greataxes, greatswords, warhammers, greathammers, wristblades, and the two-handed finesse lines: glaives, spears and quarterstaves.
[*][b]Effect ammunition[/b] — six arrows (heat, cryo, sleep gas, mire, flashbang, poison gas), four shotgun shells (incendiary, cryo, armor-piercing, takedown) and the scour slug, which rusts what your target is carrying instead of hurting them.
[*][b]44 creature colour variants[/b] — brindle dogs, black goats, cinder glowcrows. Purely cosmetic, and the ordinary animal stays the common one.
[*][b]Names, genders and pronouns[/b] — wider name pools, optional gendered endings, thirteen genders and fourteen pronoun sets, all of which Qud already had.
[*][b]A home base in Joppa[/b] — bed, storage, oven and becoming nook.
[*][b]Skill and economy retuning[/b] — more mutation and skill points, eased requirements, adjusted costs. All of it optional.
[/list]

[h1]Options[/h1]
[b]Twenty-nine settings in Qud's own options menu, under Mods.[/b] Each defaults to what the mod has always done, except where marked. Play it as tuned, or dial any of it back to vanilla.
[list]
[*]Mutation points — 16 by default, anything from 0 to 24
[*]Mutant hit points per level, and extra skill points per level
[*]Extra starting skills, eased skill requirements, retuned skill point costs
[*]Starting reputation bonus with Joppa — [b]off by default[/b]
[*]The Joppa home base building
[*]Psionic chips in loot — off closes the supply completely
[*]Chip Interface slots — a True Kin's two, and the ones on other humanoids
[*]Graded burden — [b]off by default[/b]
[*]How your own random name sounds
[*]Choose your gender at character creation, and choose your pronouns
[*]Anthro mutations - this fork's animal-trait mutations
[*]Charmed merchants still expect paying
[*]Fired arrows can be picked back up
[/list]

Psionic Adepts are unaffected throughout: their numbers are the genotype, not an addition to a vanilla one. Each option says when it takes effect.

[h1]New in 2.12.0[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]You can be made to sleep.[/b] Go about three unhurried days without it and you tire; fight for those days and you get there in half. Long enough after that and you fall down where you stand. [b]Off by default.[/b]
[*][b]Where you sleep is the decision.[/b] A settlement is safe, a bed nearly so, a sheltered spot better than bare ground. Sleep in the open with something hostile about and it finds you - it wakes, it comes, and you are told what it is.
[*][b]Sleep the whole way through and you dream[/b] - of something you did, told back in the voice the sultan histories use, or of a place you have not been, and you wake knowing where it is.
[*][b]Choose how long you sleep[/b], the way a bedroll asks, plus until rested - and each option says how many rounds it is.
[*][b]A sleep suppressor[/b], a two-point implant: nothing puts you to sleep against your will, and you tire half as fast.
[*][b]Thirteen new books[/b] to find and buy, and [b]four bookshelves[/b] that are finally about the places they stand in - Grit Gate, Hydropon, Yd Freehold and Redrock.
[*][b]Plainer names for legendary relics[/b], so the good ones stand out again.
[*][b]Companions use what you give them.[/b] Hand a follower a better axe and they work it out.
[/list]

[h1]Compatibility[/h1]
[b]Do not enable this and the original Caves of Qud Expanded at the same time.[/b] Pick one. A continuation defines the same things the original does — 36 script types with the same names — so Qud reports a type conflict and whichever loads first wins. Saves do not carry across either.

[b]Do not enable The Grand Bazaar alongside this[/b] — its content is part of this mod now, behind the Six Day Stilt option, so running both gives you two of each merchant. [b]Experience Curve Beta[/b] is still fine alongside; its script has never been able to run, whatever else is installed.

Every change this fork makes to a vanilla record is a merge, never a replacement. It does not overwrite vanilla data and should not discard what future Qud patches add. It should also play nice with most other mods. Please report any compatibility issues to me, either via Steam or via an Issue on GitHub.

[h1]Version and saves[/h1]
[b]2.12.0.[/b] Loads on 2.11.x saves - this update needs no new character. Sleep, the new books and shelves, the sleep suppressor and the plainer relic names all reach a character you are already playing. Sleep is off until you switch it on.

Coming from Mura's original, [b]start a new character[/b]: identifiers changed during the fork, and Qud writes those into save files.
